issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares numberOfTutors as type int, but the solution implementation declares the field numberOfTutors as short. This difference in attribute type can confuse students about the expected type and may lead to inconsistencies when implementing constructors/getters/setters or when tests expect int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfTutors consistent across artifacts. Change the field in the solution to int (or update the UML/problem statement to short) so that attribute type matches the specification and expected public API.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a constructor that initializes all attributes in the UML order (where numberOfTutors is specified as int). The solution's constructor accepts numberOfTutors as short. This parameter type mismatch between spec and constructor can confuse students about the correct constructor signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter type with the UML/specification. Change the constructor parameter for numberOfTutors to int (and the corresponding field to int), or update the problem statement/UML to accept short if that was intended.

issues.description: The problem/UML implies numberOfTutors is an int (so setters would reasonably accept int), but the solution's setter setNumberOfTutors uses a short parameter. This mismatch between expected setter parameter type and the solution's signature can confuse students when implementing setters or when tests expect int parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent parameter type for the setter that matches the UML/spec (change setNumberOfTutors to accept int) or update the UML to reflect the short parameter if that was intentional.
